newsitem.title: ITALY: Opposition leads vote in Milan, Turin - Abacus.
newsitem.headline: Opposition leads vote in Milan, Turin - Abacus.

text.p: Italy's main opposition alliance was ahead in mayoral races in the key northern cities of Milan and Turin after a first round of voting, forecasts showed on Monday after counting of votes got under way.

Industrialist Gabriele Albertini of the Freedom Alliance was ahead in Milan with 41.5 percent of the vote against 27.2 percent for Aldo Fumagalli of the governing centre-left Olive tree coalition, according to a projection by polling institute Abacus.
The two men will face each other in a second round run-off on May 11.
The forecast, for RAI and Mediaset television stations, was made after more than one third of votes had been counted.

The Freedom Alliance also led in Turin, Italy's northern industrial heart, where challenger Raffaele Costa was forecast by Abacus to win 43.3 percent of the vote to 34.6 percent for outgoing centre-left mayor Valentino Castellani.

Milan was the biggest prize in elections for mayors and local councils in more than 1,100 towns and cities in the first big test of electoral support since Prime Minister Romano Prodi's coalition won last April's general election. Milan newsroom +392-66102321
